home.title: andarama | ¡anda! open source 360 virtual tours
home.description: ¡anda! andarama lets me walk through panoramas. Create, publish and share 360 virtual tours with a visual editor, a WebGL viewer with VR, quizzes, LTI, SCORM and open export. Open source (EUPL-1.2): free on your own server, hosted from $2 a month.

lista.texto: From any 360 camera or from your phone. The importer reads a whole batch, sorts by the camera's numbering, renames by pattern and tiles the panoramas in your own browser, up to 32K, without waiting for any server.
Drag one scene onto another and there is a step, with its way back. In the graph every arrow is a navigation hotspot: there is no parallel data to drift out of sync.
Text, photos, videos, audio, PDFs, 3D models, questions, forms, floor plans, narration with spatial audio and translations. Seventeen hotspot types, every one of them usable inside the headset too.
A link, an iframe, your own domain or a ZIP that works on any hosting. Kiosk mode for a TV screen, SCORM for Moodle, PWA to view it offline.

editor.titulo: You edit by looking, not by filling in forms
editor.p1: The preview is the real viewer in edit mode: what you see is what gets published. Click on the photo to place a hotspot, drag to move it, draw a polygon vertex by vertex.
editor.p2: The orientation you arrive with in a room belongs to the path, not to the room: entering the living room from the hallway and from the kitchen are two different arrivals, and each one keeps its own view. The “How you get here” panel gathers them all where they can be judged: in the destination scene.
tics: Unlimited undo and redo, autosave with a warning if something fails to reach the server
Version history with per-scene and per-hotspot diffs, and restore
Command palette, keyboard shortcuts and a tabbed properties panel
Presence and soft per-scene locking when several of you edit, anchored comments with threads
Side-by-side translations with completion percentage, XLIFF and CSV
editor.alt: The Andarama editor showing a scene from Geisenheim cathedral, the scene list on the left and the arrivals panel on the right

grafo.titulo: The map of the tour, drawn
grafo.p1: A canvas with thumbnails, ports, marquee selection, minimap and auto-layout. You connect by dragging from the edge of a node and the way back is created at once. It warns about steps without a destination, without a way back, not yet placed, and about scenes nobody can reach.
grafo.p2: In Autopilot mode the same canvas draws guided tours: stops with dwell time, entry through the step that joins the two scenes and a turn towards the exit before crossing. It is what the kiosk and the auto-tour button play back.
grafo.alt: The tour graph with scenes grouped by area and connections drawn as arrows

tablero.titulo: Everything within reach, like on a desk
tablero.p1: Folders, tags, templates, a thirty-day bin and search. The cover of each tour is the panorama of its starting scene. Duplicate, rename, share with a colleague and their role.
tablero.p2: The library shows a little planet when you hover over any panorama, computed locally without touching the network, and a double click opens the photo in 360 so you can check it before using it. A single file, a selection or a whole folder can be dragged onto the graph and out come scenes.

nube.texto: No Andarama module talks directly to Cloudflare: everything goes through an adapter layer. That is why self-hosting is not a cut-down version but the very same application.

lista.texto: Workers, D1, R2, KV, Durable Objects and Analytics Engine, within the free tier for small and medium use. pnpm deploy:cloudflare and in ten minutes there is an instance.

A single file for macOS, Windows and Linux with the server, the Studio and the viewer inside. Double click, the browser opens and the data stays in your home folder. No Docker, no Node, no account with anyone.
Node and SQLite in a single image, one volume and one port. docker compose up -d. Backups with a script and the portable .andarama file.
CSP with nonces, HSTS, secure sessions, double-token CSRF, rate limits, Turnstile, sanitised SVG, Markdown and CSS, audit log and permissions checked on the server on every route.

Organisations with roles (admin, editor, contributor, reader), per-project sharing, invitations, institutional SSO via OIDC with automatic sign-up by domain, two-step verification and an admin panel with quotas and usage.

Full keyboard, visible focus, 44-pixel targets, scene-change announcements, mandatory alt text with a reviewable AI suggestion, prefers-reduced-motion, WebVTT subtitles and translations per scene and per hotspot.

EUPL-1.2, strict TypeScript across the monorepo, hundreds of unit and end-to-end tests, continuous integration with dependency audits. The tour.json format guarantees that what you export will keep opening. Code, issues and downloads are at github.com/joseluissaorin/andarama.

nombre.p1: Panorama was coined in 1791 to name “the view of everything”. Since then the suffix -rama has served for ways of looking: diorama, cyclorama, cinerama.
nombre.p2: We only changed the verb. Andar is Spanish for “to walk”: a panorama is something you look at, an andarama is something you walk through.
nombre.susurro: from “andar” + “-rama” · and yes, the yellow creature walks too

lista.a: On GitHub, under EUPL-1.2. You can read it, install it, modify it and contribute. Desktop executables and release notes are published in the releases of the same repository.

Any that produces an equirectangular photo (Insta360, Ricoh Theta, GoPro Max, Kandao…) or a phone with a panorama app. Cubemaps, partial panoramas and gigapixel flat photos work too. Tiling happens in your browser up to 32K; above that, on the server.

lista.q: Do the tours keep working if Andarama disappears?
lista.a: Yes. The exported ZIP is static and self-contained: HTML, the viewer and the tiles. Upload it to any hosting, open it from a USB stick with the single HTML file, and it keeps virtual reality. And the tour.json format is documented and versioned.

If you self-host, on your server or in your Cloudflare account. On andarama.com, in Andarama's database; Clerk only stores the account and the billing. Visitor analytics use no cookies and store no IP addresses.
Through LTI 1.3: register Andarama as an external tool, pick the tour from inside Moodle and the quiz grade goes back to the gradebook. For other LMSs, the SCORM 1.2 or 2004 package.

lista.q: Can I work with other people on the same tour?
lista.a: Yes. Organisations with roles, per-project sharing, presence and soft per-scene locking so you don't step on each other, comments anchored on the photo and version history to go back.

Any with a WebXR browser (Meta Quest, Pico, Vision Pro with Safari, a PC with a headset). Open the tour's address from the headset's browser and press the VR button. Without a headset, cardboard mode works on any phone.

That the plans are meant for one person or a small team. If usage stops looking like that, we talk before cutting anything off. And if you need something without quotas, self-hosting is free and it is the same program.

privacidad.title: Privacy and cookie policy | andarama
privacidad.description: What data andarama.com processes, with which providers (Plausible, Clerk, Cloudflare) and which cookies it uses. Explained plainly.
privacidad.lead: This page explains what data andarama.com processes, why and with whom. It is written to be read, not to tick a box.

secciones.html: José Luis Saorín Ferrer, author of Andarama, reachable at jl@joseluissaorin.com. Andarama is an open-source program (EUPL-1.2); andarama.com is the hosted instance he maintains.

To know how many people visit the site we use Plausible, a European service that sets no cookies, stores no IP addresses and does not identify anyone across visits. It counts page views and a few anonymous events (for example, that a tool was used). That is why there is no cookie banner: there is nothing to accept.

Tours published with Andarama carry the same kind of analytics: aggregated visits, scenes and hotspots, without cookies and without IPs.

If you create an account on app.andarama.com, sign-up, sign-in and plan billing are handled by Clerk. Clerk stores your email, your name if you give it, your sign-in method and billing details; to keep you signed in it uses technical cookies, which are essential for the application to work. Tours, media and everything you create are stored in Andarama's own database, not in Clerk.

andarama.com is served from Cloudflare (Workers, D1, R2 and KV). Cloudflare processes requests as a data processor and may keep technical logs for a limited time for security. The media you upload is stored in R2, in European data centres whenever possible.

The 360 viewer, the little planet maker and the cubemap converter run entirely in your browser. The images you open with them are not uploaded to any server: they never leave your computer. We only record, without identifying you, that the tool was used.

If you write from the contact form, your own email program opens: the message goes from your account to ours and is used only to reply to you. Accounts receive transactional email (verification, invitations, plan notices), never advertising.

You can request access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection by writing to jl@joseluissaorin.com. Accounts can be deleted from within the application, and everything you create can be exported at any time as a ZIP or as an .andarama file. If you believe something is not being done right, you can lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD).
If this policy changes, the date is noted here. Last revision: September 2026.

visor.title: Free 360 photo viewer online: view 360 photos in your browser | andarama
visor.description: Free online 360 photo viewer. Open an equirectangular photo (JPG or PNG) and look around in 360 with fullscreen and VR, without uploading anything to any server.
visor.h1: 360 photo viewer online: view your equirectangular photo in the browser
visor.lead: Pick a 360 photo and it appears right here as if you were wearing a headset: drag to look around, scroll to zoom, fullscreen and virtual reality if your browser has WebXR. Nothing is uploaded: the viewer is Andarama's own engine running on your computer.
visor.rv_no: This browser has no WebXR. Open this same page from the browser of a Meta Quest, Pico or Vision Pro headset.
visor.cuerpo:
What a 360 photo is and why it looks wrong in a normal viewer

A 360 (equirectangular) photo is a sphere unrolled onto a 2:1 rectangle: the 360 degrees of turn along the width and the 180 degrees from top to bottom along the height. Opened in an ordinary photo viewer it looks stretched, with the floor and the sky distorted and straight lines bent into curves. A 360 viewer wraps the image back onto a sphere and puts you at the centre, so you look around as if you were there.

How to use this online 360 viewer

  1. Press “Choose a 360 photo” or drop the file onto the dotted area. It takes the JPG and PNG files produced by Insta360, Ricoh Theta, GoPro Max, Kandao, phone panorama apps or any stitching software.
  2. Drag with the mouse or a finger to turn; use the wheel or pinch to zoom in and out; with the keyboard, the arrow keys.
  3. The fullscreen button fills the monitor; the headset button starts a virtual reality session if the browser has WebXR (Meta Quest, Pico, Vision Pro with Safari or a PC with a headset).

Nothing gets uploaded

The image never travels to a server: the browser decodes it and the WebGL engine paints it on your graphics card. You can use it with private or client photos without them leaving your computer. And since there is no upload, there is no waiting either: an 8K photo opens in a couple of seconds.

View 360 photos on PC, phone and headset

This viewer works in any modern browser: Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge, on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. On a phone you can turn the view with the gyroscope. On a VR headset, the same page offers the enter-VR button and the photo wraps the whole room.

What it doesn't do (and where to do it)

It doesn't store the photo or generate a link to share it: that would require uploading it somewhere. If you want to share a 360 photo by link, embed it on your website, connect several into a tour or add hotspots, that is what Andarama does, and you can try it free for fourteen days.

faq.q: Which formats does the viewer accept?
faq.a: Equirectangular JPG and PNG files with a 2:1 ratio, which is what every 360 camera and stitching program produces. It also opens panoramas that don't cover the full 360 degrees, though there will be a black band.
The limit is your browser's memory. 8K photos (8192×4096) open without trouble on any computer; above 16K the image is reduced automatically so the graphics card can handle it.

faq.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything happens in your browser: the photo is read from disk, decoded and drawn with WebGL. We only record, without identifying you, that the tool was used.

faq.q: Can I view the photo with a VR headset?
faq.a: Yes, if the browser has WebXR: open this page from the browser of a Meta Quest, Pico or Vision Pro and press the headset button. On a phone without WebXR you can turn the view with the gyroscope.

faq.q: How do I share a 360 photo by link?
faq.a: This viewer doesn't store it. To get a link, embed it on a website or connect several photos into a tour, create an account on Andarama: the trial lasts fourteen days and asks for no card.

planeta.title: Little planet maker online, free | andarama
planeta.description: Turn a 360 photo into a little planet (tiny planet) and download it as PNG. Free, in the browser, without uploading the image anywhere.
planeta.h1: Little planet maker: turn your 360 photo into a tiny planet
planeta.lead: Upload an equirectangular photo and out comes the planet: the ground at the centre, the sky all around. Rotate it, open or close the world and download it as PNG at whatever size you like. All in your browser.
planeta.cuerpo:
What a little planet is

A little planet (or tiny planet) is a stereographic projection of a 360 photo: take the whole sphere, rest it on the ground and project it onto a plane from the zenith. The result is a disc with the ground at the centre, buildings and trees growing outwards and the sky wrapping around the edge. It is the most photogenic way to show, in a single image, everything that surrounded the camera.

How to make a little planet with this tool

  1. Choose an equirectangular photo (2:1 JPG or PNG) from any 360 camera or panorama app.
  2. Adjust the rotation to decide what ends up at the top of the planet and the opening to bring the horizon closer or further away. The planet is recalculated instantly.
  3. Pick the output size and the background (transparent to compose it over something else) and download the PNG.

Tips for a good planet

Photos with a clean nadir (no tripod, no hand) work best, because the centre of the disc is precisely the ground. Scenes with an open horizon and an interesting sky make the nicest planets; squares, courtyards and summits are winning cases. If the original is tilted, fix it first: the projection exaggerates any lean.

No upload, no watermark

The calculation runs pixel by pixel in your browser with the same routine Andarama's media library uses to show its thumbnails. The photo never leaves your computer and the PNG you download is yours, with no watermark and no resolution limit beyond your machine's memory.

faq.a: Anything between 512 and 4096 pixels per side. Final sharpness depends on the original photo: an 8K equirectangular gives perfectly crisp 4096 px planets.
Yes: download at 2048 or 4096 px with a white or black background and upload it as a square image. The transparent background is handy for compositing over another design.

faq.q: Can I make the planet inside out (sky at the centre)?
faq.a: Not yet from this tool. That is the “tunnel” projection; if you would like it, write to us and we will add it.
No. It is computed in your browser and never travels to any server.

cubemap.title: Equirectangular to cubemap converter online (and back) | andarama
cubemap.description: Free equirectangular panorama to cubemap converter: six PNG faces or a ZIP, and cubemap to equirectangular. In the browser, nothing uploaded.
cubemap.h1: Equirectangular to cubemap (and cubemap to equirectangular)
cubemap.lead: Upload a 2:1 panorama and get the six cube faces as PNG, separately or in a ZIP. Or the other way round: pick six faces and an equirectangular gets stitched. Everything is computed in your browser.
cubemap.cuerpo:
What a cubemap is and what it is for

A cubemap represents the surroundings with six square images, one per face of a cube: front, back, left, right, up and down. It is the format expected by 3D engines (Unity, Unreal, Godot, Three.js, Babylon), game skyboxes, reflection maps and many 360 viewers, because each face is a normal texture without the equirectangular's distortion at the poles.

How to convert an equirectangular to a cubemap

  1. Choose the equirectangular panorama (2:1 JPG or PNG).
  2. Pick the face size. The rule is the panorama's width divided by four: an 8192 px equirectangular gives 2048 px faces.
  3. Download the six faces separately or as a ZIP named f, b, l, r, u, d (the Marzipano and krpano convention) or with your engine's naming.

And from cubemap to equirectangular

The reverse path is here too: choose the six faces and the tool stitches them into a single 2:1 panorama ready for any 360 viewer, for social media or for Andarama. Useful to recover a game skybox, a Blender render in cube format or a panorama from a camera that exports faces.

How it is computed

For every pixel of every face, a direction is traced from the centre of the cube, converted to longitude and latitude, and the matching point of the equirectangular is read. It is the same geometry Andarama's tiler uses to prepare tours, executed here on a Canvas inside your browser. No image is uploaded anywhere.

faq.q: Which face size should I choose?
faq.a: The equirectangular's width divided by four: 4096 wide, 1024 px faces; 8192, 2048 px faces. A larger size adds no detail, only weight.

faq.q: In which order and with which names do the faces come out?
faq.a: By default with the Marzipano and krpano convention (f, b, l, r, u, d). You can also pick the Unity and Three.js one (px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz).
